ED01: Extended Data Fig. 1 | Identification of studies reporting AlphaFold use. Candidate work records were retrieved using keywords and citations to four initial seed resources, with supplementary retrieval shown separately. Abstract or full-text evidence was assessed for use of AF models or predicted structures in the study’s own methods, analyses, experiments, development or evaluation. Citation, background discussion or future plans alone did not establish use; insufficient evidence was retained as unknown. Units and observation periods are labelled at each stage. Full dispositions and study consolidation are detailed in Supplementary Fig. S1 and Table S1.
ED02: Extended Data Fig. 2 | Geographic diffusion of AF research. a, Countries and regions classified by their first observed AF publication: before July 2021 (Pre-AF2), July 2021–April 2024 (AF2), or May 2024 onward (AF3). Grey indicates no observed publication; near-white areas fall outside the country-code registry. The timeline summarizes milestones in model development, database availability, code and weights, and scientific recognition.  b,c, Cumulative participating countries and regions (b) and monthly new participants (c) during 2020–2025. Cumulative counts include one country first observed before 2020; earlier portions of the time axis are left blank. Dashed lines mark the July 2021 and May 2024 phase boundaries. Milestones provide historical context rather than evidence of causal effects.
ED03: Extended Data Fig. 3 | National AF-use intensity and concentration. a, Relative AF intensity for the ten largest baseline producers (2015–2019), comparing 2021 and 2025 and showing annual trajectories. R=1 indicates equal national shares of AF and eligible output; axes are logarithmic. b, AF-output shares of the top five and top ten countries, ranked separately each year. c, Stacked bars and heatmap show fractional AF output shares for the ten leading countries by total 2020–2025 credit; remaining countries are pooled as Other. Shares exclude unknown-country credit. Row swatches identify bar segments; cell shading indicates share magnitude.
ED04: Extended Data Fig. 4 | Institutional sample construction and timing of first observed AlphaFold publication. a, Sequential construction of the institutional sample. Institutions were excluded for unknown or multiple baseline countries, collapsed or empty within-country publication-output tertiles, or fewer than 20 institutions in any tertile. The final sample comprises 48,010 institutions in 68 countries. b, Annual counts of institutions with a first observed AlphaFold (AF) publication in 2020–2025, restricted to institutions with a resolved first-publication date. First observed publication refers to participation recorded in the study corpus and does not necessarily identify the onset of AF use.
ED05: Extended Data Fig. 5 | Country-specific changes in institutional AF coverage disparities. a, Annual coverage ratios (Lower / Higher institutions). b, Annual coverage gaps (Higher − Lower institutions; percentage points). Open and filled circles denote 2021 and 2025; lines connect defined endpoints. Purple shades distinguish national publication-output groups: High (n = 23), Middle (n = 22) and Low (n = 23). Institutional groups are defined by within-country publication output in 2015–2019. Countries follow the same order in both panels. Asterisks in a mark 24 countries with undefined 2021 ratios (0/0), where both institutional groups had zero AF coverage; only their 2025 endpoints are shown.
ED06: Extended Data Fig. 6 | International collaboration, team size and authorship sample retention. a, Annual international co-authorship among studies with identifiable country information, 2020–2025; the bracket marks the 2025 AF–non-AF difference. b, Median observed author counts with interquartile ranges for country-known and international studies. The 2020 AF samples contain nine and three studies, respectively. c, Study counts through role eligibility, complete author-country information and common-support restrictions; percentages indicate retention from the preceding stage. d, Author-complete retention among international studies, pooled across 2020–2025 before common-support restriction. National groups are fixed using 2015–2019 output; Outside denotes unclassified countries. Group memberships may overlap. Red circles denote AF and blue squares non-AF. Interquartile ranges describe variation among studies, not confidence intervals (Methods M6; Supplementary Table S7).
ED07: Extended Data Fig. 7 | Institutional zero-authorship credit and observed participation. The unit of analysis is the country–institution pair. a, Percentages of eligible units with no first-author (left) or last-author (right) credit, by participating-study count; numbers below show role-specific sample sizes. b, Observed percentages (filled symbols) and reference expectations (open symbols) when two distinct authors are selected uniformly from each observed team. Whiskers show central 95% conditional reference ranges from 2,000 joint allocations; these are not bootstrap confidence intervals. Red circles denote AF and blue squares non-AF. This separate opportunity analysis includes 5,425 AF and 477,291 non-AF studies with the required author identifiers. Role-specific unit denominators are shown in b. Institutional representation distributions are reported in Supplementary Table S9a, b (Methods M7; Supplementary Table S9c).
ED08: Extended Data Fig. 8 | Institutional collaboration across output groups. Analyses include 5,055 AF and 331,101 screen-negative reference (non-AF) internationally co-authored studies (2020–2025) with institutional affiliations for all observed authors. Non-AF studies are weighted to match AF by publication year, subfield and document type. Groups reflect within-country output in 2015–2019; Other includes unclassified institutions. Each study contributes one credit, divided equally among pairs of distinct institutions linked by distinct authors. a,b, Co-publication links in AF (a) and non-AF research (b) Sector colours identify institutional groups; sector sizes and ribbon widths are proportional to endpoint and pair credit, respectively. Within-group ribbons are pale. c, Partner composition within each focal group, counting both endpoints of each pair; labels show higher-output partner shares. d, AF–non-AF differences in these shares, in percentage points (pp), with conditional 95% whole-study bootstrap intervals (2,000 replicates); the dashed line marks zero.
ED09: Extended Data Fig. 9 | Absolute publication outcomes and sensitivity of journal comparisons. a, b, Cumulative distributions of institution-level AF and matched non-AF mean journal percentiles (2020–2025; a) and 12-month citation percentiles (2020–2024; b). Institutions receive equal weight; solid and dashed lines denote AF and non-AF. c, Mean journal-percentile differences from 2015–2019 publications matched within institution, subfield and document type, among eligible institutions with historical references; n denotes institutions. d, Journal-percentile differences using all eligible comparisons within each year window (available) or records supporting both journal and citation comparisons (shared). Samples differ across specifications. Whiskers in c, d show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings; dashed lines mark zero. Groups reflect within-country institutional output in 2015–2019; shading highlights the Lower group (Methods M8).
ED10: Extended Data Fig. 10 | Sample selection and adjusted network associations. a, Baseline connectivity across samples; points show medians, lines interquartile ranges, and n institution counts. b, Group-specific own-connectivity slopes before and after adjustment, restricted to partner-assessable records, and with partner connectivity added; the latter two models use identical records. c, Final-model partner-connectivity slopes, assumed common across groups; n denotes institutions. Columns in b,c show journal and 12-month citation outcomes. Models adjust for baseline output, country, year, field and document type. Slopes are per unit of ln(1 + degree) in b and per ten partner-percentile points in c. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings with fixed networks. d, Partner-information availability across 2020–2025 AF study–institution links; n denotes links. Groups and networks use 2015–2019 records (Methods M8).
Fig01: Fig. 1 | Country-level concentration of AF and non-AF research, 2021-2025. a, Annual output Gini coefficients for AF and non-AF output across 227 countries and regions, including those with zero output. Each study contributes 1/k credit to each of its k observed countries. Shading shows conditional 95% whole-study bootstrap intervals from 1,000 replicates. The main comparison starts in 2021 because only 11 AF studies were identified in 2020 (Supplementary Fig. S3a). b, Raw and matched AF-minus-non-AF Gini gaps. Matched gaps subtract the mean Gini of 2,000 non-AF samples per year, matched to AF study counts within primary-subfield and document-type strata. Shading shows conditional 95% bootstrap intervals for raw gaps; bars show central 95% matched ranges with AF output held fixed. The bracket indicates that approximately 66% of the net raw narrowing occurred during 2021–2022.  c, Changes in Gini gaps, calculated as 2025 minus 2021: −0.0144 for the raw gap (conditional 95% bootstrap interval, −0.0232 to −0.0105) and +0.0026 for the matched gap (central 95% matched range, −0.0093 to +0.0134). Negative values indicate narrowing; positive values indicate widening. Matched ranges reflect variation across non-AF samples with AF output held fixed and are not full confidence intervals.
Fig02: Fig. 2 | Institutional coverage and subsequent participation. Institutions are grouped by within-country publication output in 2015–2019, with group membership fixed. a, Cumulative coverage: the percentage of institutions with at least one confirmed AF publication by each year, averaged equally across 68 countries and regions. Institutions without confirmed AF publications remain in the denominators. The inset enlarges lower-output coverage. b, Annual lower-to-higher coverage ratio (R, upper) and higher-minus-lower coverage gap (G, lower), calculated from equally weighted country means. Increasing R indicates relative catch-up; increasing G indicates a widening absolute gap. Solid and dashed lines show observed and expected gaps, respectively; shading shows the central 95% conditional reference range. c, Activities documented in initial AF studies. Numbers give percentages among institutions with sufficient evidence to assess each activity, with supported/assessable counts below. Activities can overlap, and evidence from co-authored studies does not identify which institution performed the work. d, Repeat publication within twelve calendar months of entry, excluding initial and same-day studies. Filled circles show observed rates; diamonds and horizontal bars show reference expectations and central 95% conditional ranges. Dotted extensions end at rates obtained if all registered unresolved follow-up cases were confirmed. Group sample sizes are shown beside the axis. References condition on observed publication and affiliation structures, with entry dates additionally held fixed in d; their ranges do not represent causal-effect confidence intervals (Methods M3–M5).
Fig03: Fig. 3 | Authorship representation under alternative participation benchmarks. Analyses include 5,087 AF and 332,760 screen-negative reference (non-AF) international studies on common support, with non-AF studies weighted to match AF across 173 year–subfield–document-type cells. Country groups are fixed by 2015–2019 national output; outside-group credit remains in global denominators. a, First- and last-author representation ratios, RR=authorship-credit shareparticipaiton-credit share, under fractional country-output and team-author benchmarks. Red and blue bars denote AF and non-AF; the dashed line marks  RR=1.b, AF–non-AF differences in representation, ∆RR=RRAF-RRnon-AF, across benchmarks. Solid lines with filled circles denote first authorship; dashed lines with open triangles denote last authorship. Points are horizontally offset for clarity; the dashed horizontal line marks zero. Panels share country-group columns, with low-output countries shaded. Whiskers show conditional 95% whole-study bootstrap intervals (2,000 replicates). Paired benchmark changes appear in Supplementary Fig. S10a and Supplementary Table S8b.
Fig04: Fig. 4 | First–last authorship pairings in international research. The cohort, common support and weights are identical to Fig. 3. a, Fractional pairing credit by country and institutional correspondence. AF is red and non-AF blue; shades distinguish categories. Same-institution pairs share a country and known institution. Same-country pairings with unresolved institutional correspondence remain included in the totals (AF, 0.10%; non-AF, 0.07%). b, Observed pairings between national output groups defined using 2015–2019 publications, with first authors on the left and last authors on the right. Purple shades identify output groups; ribbons are red for AF, blue for non-AF and grey for pairings involving Outside. Ribbon widths represent fractional shares, summing to 100% within each corpus; labels show high–high shares. Within-group pairings may involve different countries. c, AF observed-minus-expected shares (left) and the AF–non-AF difference in these deviations (right). Expectations derive from uniformly selecting two distinct authors from each observed team. Both matrices share a zero-centered scale in percentage points: red indicates positive values and blue negative values. Conditional 95% whole-study bootstrap intervals for the direct higher–higher and lower–lower contrasts include zero. Full estimates and intervals are reported in Supplementary Table S10 (Methods M7).
Fig05: Fig. 5 | Publication outcomes among AF participants and institutional coverage. a, b, AF–non-AF differences in journal percentiles for 2020–2025 (a) and twelve-month citation percentiles for 2020–2024 (b), matched within institution, publication year, subfield and document type. Left, means weighted equally across institutions, with conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings. Right, institution-level distributions; open circles mark medians, thick lines indicate interquartile ranges, and n denotes institutions. Samples are outcome-specific; dashed lines mark zero. c, Percentage of baseline institutions with at least one confirmed AF study meeting the journal-percentile threshold of 75 (left) or twelve-month citation-percentile threshold of 90 (right) during 2020–2024. Small open circles show country-specific rates; larger filled symbols and numerical labels show equally weighted means across 68 countries. Denominators retain all 48,010 baseline institutions, including nonparticipants. Pale shading highlights lower-output institutions. Throughout, groups are fixed by within-country publication output in 2015–2019 (Methods M8).
Fig06: Fig. 6 | Collaboration networks and relative AF outcomes. a, b, Institution-level AF–non-AF differences in journal and twelve-month citation percentiles plotted against own baseline connectivity (a) and AF partners’ mean baseline degree percentile (b). Rows show within-country institutional output groups defined by 2015–2019 publications; network measures use collaborations from the same period. Points represent institutions; lines show unadjusted, equally weighted linear fits restricted to observed support. Dashed lines mark zero. Labels report slopes (β), conditional 95% intervals and institution counts (n). Slopes are per unit of ln(1+degree)in a and per ten partner-percentile points in b, where degree counts distinct institutional collaborators and partner measures exclude the focal institution. Non-AF references are screen-negative studies matched within institution, publication year, subfield and document type.
S01: Supplementary Fig. S1 | Corpus construction and supplementary retrieval. a, Records retained after publication-type filtering, study linkage and restriction to 2020–2025. b, Review of additional retrieval leads; A/B submissions comprise 154 full-text and 402 abstract packets. The 516 routed C reviews overlap with A/B submissions. c, Supplementary decisions and their contribution to the final AF sample. Version linkage converts 74 positive works into 73 additional studies: 70 from the initial update and three added subsequently. The initial 29,127 candidates and supplementary retrieval form separate routes to evidence assessment (Extended Data Fig. 1). Work-record and study counts are distinct; the analysis corpus is not a screening-stage count.
S02: Supplementary Fig. S2 | Pilot annotation and production-label agreement. a, Human review of 150 deliberately selected candidate works yielded 122 resolved labels and 28 unresolved cases. The human reference combined 41 exact agreements and 109 adjudications across two annotation workbooks. b, Production labels compared with resolved human labels; cells show work counts. Precision was 98.10% (103/105) and recall 100% (103/103). Unknown predictions remain separate from non-use. This selected pilot was not an independent held-out validation and does not assess retrieval completeness.
S03: Supplementary Fig. S3 | Growth and subfield distribution of AF research. a, Annual confirmed AF-study counts. b, Subfield shares of AF studies (n = 16,414) and the eligible corpus (n = 2,714,594), pooled over 2020–2025. c, AF studies as a percentage of eligible studies within each subfield and year. The five largest AF subfields by total study count are fixed across panels; Other pools the remaining subfields. The eligible corpus includes AF studies. The 2020 AF sample contains 11 studies.
S04: Supplementary Fig. S4 | Sensitivity of national concentration comparisons. a, AF–non-AF Gini gaps after matching study counts alone, adding subfield and document-type composition, or further restricting to studies with known country information. b, Changes in matched gaps from 2021 or 2022 to 2025; negative values indicate narrowing. Shading in a and whiskers in b show central 95% ranges across 2,000 non-AF matching draws with AF output held fixed, rather than full confidence intervals. c, Studies with identifiable country information as a percentage of each corpus. Non-AF denotes screen-negative reference studies.
S05: Supplementary Fig. S5 | Institutional coverage under alternative classifications and continuous publication rank. a,b, Cumulative AF coverage using within-country groups defined by baseline linked-author counts (a) or institutional-partner counts (b). Both analyses retain the same 47,910 institutions in 67 countries, with metric-specific group assignments fixed across 2020–2025. c, Coverage by within-country publication percentile in 2025 across 48,010 institutions in 68 countries. The curve is a country-adjusted spline standardized equally across countries; dashed segments extend beyond at least one country’s observed rank range. Open circles show equally weighted country means within rank bins, containing 44–68 countries. All baseline measures use 2015–2019 records. Estimates are descriptive; no confidence intervals are shown.
S06: Supplementary Fig. S6 | Reference checks for institutional coverage disparities. a–c, Annual coverage gaps between Higher and Lower institutional groups within High-, Middle- and Low-output countries, respectively, averaged equally across countries. Solid and dashed lines show observed and expected gaps; shading shows central 95% conditional ranges from 5,000 AF-label allocations. d, Observed and expected gap changes under minimum within-country group sizes of 10, 20 or 30 institutions. e, Annual gaps under equal-country and pooled-institution weighting. f, Observed minus expected gap changes under the primary reference and additional document-type or fixed team-size strata; negative values indicate less widening than expected. Filled circles and open diamonds in d show observed and expected values. Points in d,f are shown without intervals. All gaps are in percentage points (pp); reference ranges are not effect confidence intervals. Groups use 2015–2019 records.
S07: Supplementary Fig. S7 | Institutional AF coverage by national income. a–d, Cumulative coverage in 2020–2025 by World Bank FY2020 income group, averaged equally across countries. Within-country institutional groups use 2015–2019 output; all 48,010 baseline institutions remain in the denominators. Labels show 2025 coverage and n denotes countries. The low-income group contains only Ethiopia and Uganda. e, Observed minus expected change in the annual Higher–Lower coverage gap from 2021 to 2025. Bars show zero-centred 95% conditional reference ranges from 5,000 AF-label allocations; points show observed residuals. These ranges are not confidence intervals around the points. Negative values indicate less gap widening than expected. Panel e uses annual coverage; a–d use cumulative coverage.
S08: Supplementary Fig. S8 | Activity evidence and author continuity. a, Changes in activity evidence between institutions’ initial and first subsequent AF studies. Bars show the shares of assessable paired institutions; labels give counts and paired n gives the denominator for each activity. Activities overlap and are recorded at the study level, not attributed to individual institutions. Evidence not re-established at follow-up does not imply confirmed non-use; independent activity-label validation remains incomplete. b, Institution-affiliated author overlap among 1,312 assessable institutions out of 2,137 confirmed repeaters; 825 remain unclassified. Initial authors only does not require every initial author to return. Author overlap does not establish knowledge transfer or team replacement.
S09: Supplementary Fig. S9 | Repeat publication and follow-up opportunities. The fixed complete-12-month cohort contains 4,955 institutions: Lower, 176; Middle, 630; Higher, 3,903; and unclassified, 246. a, Distributions of distinct studies published within 12 months of entry (medians: 2, 7 and 53 for Lower, Middle and Higher); the horizontal scale is linear near zero and logarithmic above one. b, Observed minus expected repeat AF publication under primary entry constraints, coarser strata omitting country sets, and relaxed constraints fixing entry AF studies only. c, Observed and expected repeat AF publication in the next complete calendar year. Whiskers are 95% conditional allocation ranges, not confidence intervals. d, Confirmed repeat publication at 3, 6 and 12 months in the same cohort. Open circles additionally include registered unresolved potential follow-ups; dotted extensions are not confidence intervals or bounds on all unobserved AF use. All includes unclassified institutions. Institutional groups use baseline within-country output.
S10: Supplementary Fig. S10 | Authorship benchmarks and eligibility sensitivity. a, Paired change in the AF–non-AF representation contrast when replacing fractional country output with team-author credit: C = ΔRR(team) - ΔRR(output). Positive values indicate an upward shift in the contrast. National groups use 2015–2019 output; Outside comprises countries outside these groups. b, c, Low-group first- and last-author ΔRR under the team-author benchmark across eligibility and support criteria. Each variant rebuilds common support and target weights; the primary analysis requires ≥5 non-AF studies per cell. Whiskers show conditional 95% whole-study bootstrap intervals (2,000 replicates); dashed lines mark zero. Sensitivity analyses are not independent replications.
S11: Supplementary Fig. S11 | Authorship representation by national income. AF–non-AF differences in first- and last-author representation (ΔRR) within the original 68-country scope (a, b) and across 213 income-classified countries and regions (c, d), using fractional country-output and team-author benchmarks. Income groups follow World Bank FY2020 classifications; the original-scope low-income group contains only Ethiopia and Uganda. All panels use the same 5,087 AF and 332,760 non-AF studies and publication-year, subfield and document-type weights. Outside-scope credit remains in global denominators. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 2,000 shared whole-study bootstrap replicates; dashed lines mark zero.
S12: Supplementary Fig. S12 | Team-composition expectations for first–last authorship. Expected pairing shares for AF (a) and composition-standardized non-AF studies (b), and observed-minus-expected shares for non-AF studies (c). Expectations select two distinct authors uniformly within each study’s team. Rows denote first-author and columns last-author national output groups, fixed using 2015–2019 publications; Outside denotes countries outside the fixed groups. Analyses use 5,087 AF and 332,760 non-AF studies on common support. Shares are percentages; deviations are percentage points. Within-group pairings may span countries. Observed shares and AF deviations are shown in Fig. 4.
S13: Supplementary Fig. S13 | Publication-outcome sample support. a, AF studies and institutions in the journal (2020–2025), 12-month citation (2020–2024) and common 2020–2024 outcome samples with matched non-AF references. Study counts cover the full eligible population; institution counts show classified baseline groups. These are parallel samples, not successive exclusions. b, Outcome-sample coverage of fixed baseline institutions (Lower, 17,602; Middle, 14,720; Higher, 15,688). c, Unavailable outcomes or references among 2020–2025 AF study–institution links; reasons overlap and cannot be added. d, Institutions with exactly one eligible AF study, as a percentage of each outcome sample. Colours identify within-country baseline institutional groups; filled circles denote journal and open diamonds citation samples.
S14: Supplementary Fig. S14 | Weighting, matching and outcome-sample sensitivity. a, AF–non-AF differences under equal institution, country, study and institution-year weighting. b, Comparisons requiring ≥5 non-AF references per cell or matching publication time by quarter or month. c, Citation differences in the maximum and common 2020–2024 outcome samples. d, Absolute outcomes after standardizing institutional groups to a common composition target; point estimates only. Colours identify within-country baseline output groups. Whiskers in a–c show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings. Matching rules can change sample support; sample sizes are retained in the accompanying data. Journal year-window comparisons appear in Extended Data Fig. 9d.
S15: Supplementary Fig. S15 | Outcome measurement and citation-window sensitivity. a, AF–non-AF differences in high-journal shares using mean-category percentile thresholds or supplier-reported best-category Q1. b, Differences in shares reaching the 90th or 95th citation percentile. Requiring ≥50 or ≥200 reference studies per percentile cell changed these estimates by <0.03 percentage points (accompanying data). c, Journal-percentile differences with and without multidisciplinary journals. d, Twelve- and twenty-four-month citation differences using identical AF studies and jointly assessable reference support; n denotes institutions. Colours identify within-country baseline output groups. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings; dashed lines mark zero. Panels a, b report percentage points; c, d report percentile points.
S16: Supplementary Fig. S16 | Annual publication outcomes and qualifying-study coverage. a,b, Annual AF–non-AF differences in journal and 12-month citation percentiles. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings; open points denote fewer than ten institutions. Unavailable estimates remain missing; points are slightly offset horizontally. c, Qualifying-study coverage after 12 and 24 months in the same mature entrant cohort (Lower, n = 48; Middle, 190; Higher, 2,489). d, Equal-country mean AF and qualifying-journal coverage in the fixed baseline population. Qualifying thresholds are journal ≥75th and citation ≥90th percentile. Filled/open endpoints in c, d show confirmed/possible recorded-status bounds, not confidence intervals or bounds on all unobserved AF use. Colours identify within-country baseline output groups.
S17: Supplementary Fig. S17 | Historical comparison support. a, Median numbers of same-institution, subfield and document-type studies in 2015–2019, across AF study–institution links with observed historical support; the vertical scale is logarithmic. b, AF-minus-historical-reference journal-percentile differences under increasing minimum historical-study requirements, starting from the common 2020–2024 outcome sample. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings. Open points have fewer than ten institutions and no interval; n denotes retained institutions. The Lower group retains 23, 7, 1 and 0 institutions; no estimate is plotted at zero support. Colours identify within-country baseline output groups. These historical comparisons differ from the contemporaneous matched non-AF comparisons.
S18: Supplementary Fig. S18 | Network sensitivity checks. Own-network slopes under alternative measures (a), historical windows (b), boundaries (c) and large-team exclusions (d). Common denotes fixed-intersection comparisons; large teams have >20 institutions in the full observed roster. e, Partner scores using complete or partially scored partner sets. f, Adjusted own-connectivity slopes before and after high-leverage exclusions. Outcomes are institutional AF–non-AF percentile differences. Colours identify within-country baseline output groups; filled circles/open diamonds denote journal/12-month citation outcomes. Whiskers show conditional 95% intervals from 5,000 shared-study re-weightings with networks fixed. NE marks the inestimable Lower-group partner-maximum citation model. High-leverage exclusions retain only five/two Lower institutions for journal/citation outcomes, shown without intervals. Slopes are per unit ln(1 + network measure) in a–d, per ten partner-percentile points in e and per unit ln(1 + degree) in f.
S19: Supplementary Fig. S19 | Absolute publication outcomes and prior institutional connectivity. Institution-level mean journal percentiles (a, c, e) and 12-month citation percentiles (b, d, f) for AF studies and their matched non-AF references, plotted against 2015–2019 collaboration degree. Rows show Lower, Middle and Higher within-country baseline output groups. Each institution contributes one AF point and one reference point at the same connectivity value; n denotes institutions. Samples match the own-connectivity analyses in Fig. 6a. Axes are shared; point opacity decreases in larger samples to limit overplotting. These absolute outcomes complement the within-institution AF–non-AF differences in Fig. 6.
